text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- PM watches election fever rise: Prophets favour June 2, Quebec Liberals cancel May gathering just in case.
- Liberals score low on voters' big issues: Poll shows only one positive mark.
- Manitoba hunkers down for flood: Deluge of century may hit province.
- De Klerk named in secret-war report: Commission hears of third force.
- Mystery death, secret life astound de Guzman's wife: Spouse learned of Bre-X geologist's other wives after suicide.
- Wheat export cap rejected: Trade Minister says Canada will not limit shipments to the United States amid farmers' call for quotas.
- Repap close to the financial brink: Sources say company must find buyer or obtain more credit next week - otherwise, it could go under.
- Royal Bank to lend Eaton's up to C$99 million: Money to help keep 85 stores operating.
- OSC hunts for trading reports: Probe to see if Bre-X insiders sold shares before price fall.
- New clues in Bre-X assay mystery: Area where 13 kilogram samples were bagged presented best opportunity for tampering at Busang site, experts say.
- Eaton's credit line extended to C$200 million.
